title: Projected Impact on Export Competitiveness from Strengthening of Singapore Dollar
what_it_is: Projected Impact on Export Competitiveness from Strengthening of Singapore Dollar

sections.label: MAS monetary policy tightening
sections.summary: MAS has tightened monetary policy three times since October 2021, when it shifted to a slight appreciation of the policy band.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: MAS has tightened its monetary policy stance three times since October 2021, when the Authority shifted to a slight appreciation of the policy band within which the exchange rate is managed.

sections.label: Core inflation peaking forecast
sections.summary: MAS expects core inflation to keep rising in the coming months before peaking at around 4% in Q3 this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: MAS expects core inflation to continue to rise in the coming months before peaking at around 4% in Q3 this year.

sections.label: Singapore GDP growth forecast
sections.summary: MAS expects the Singapore economy to grow at an above-trend pace of around 3% to 5% this year, reaffirmed in its April 2022 statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In the absence of further disruptions caused by the Ukraine war or a severe setback in trajectory of the pandemic, the Singapore economy should grow at an above-trend pace for the second consecutive year at around 3% to 5% this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The April 2022 Monetary Policy Statement has reaffirmed MAS' assessment of this GDP growth forecast range, barring significant external shocks that I mentioned earlier.

sections.label: Stronger Singapore dollar appreciation question
sections.summary: MAS does not give advance guidance on future exchange rate policy and will focus on medium-term price stability, avoiding sudden large policy shifts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am wondering whether a stronger appreciation of the Singapore dollar may be warranted and if this is a consideration that MAS will seriously consider in the months ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We do not give advance guidance of future exchange rate policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But, as I mentioned earlier on, MAS will continue to focus on medium-term price stability and avoid sudden large shifts in policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But the key thing is that because of the way in which our exports and imports are structured, the impact on price competitiveness vis-à-vis our exports is not heavily affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The second part is that we will continue to strengthen our companies, as well as the export competitiveness, but I think the appreciation of the slope will help our exports to remain competitive in the long run.
